name: Miniature Circuit Breaker
tagline: The over-current guard on every final circuit — trips when current exceeds its rating.
terminals: Fix aperture on top / Bottom DIN clip
parts: Toggle lever — reset after a trip
DIN-rail clip — snap onto the board
safety: Match the breaker to the cable: a 16 A MCB needs at least 1.5 mm² on a standard loop. Oversizing the breaker is how a cable melts before the trip.

points.label: Toggle lever
points.detail: The lever is the manual disconnect — flip it down to isolate a circuit for service. After a trip it springs to a middle position between ON and OFF and must be pushed fully down, then clicked up to reset.

points.label: Thermal trip (bimetal)
points.detail: A bimetal strip heats with sustained current and bends until it trips the mechanism. This is the slow curve that protects against overload — a 22 A load on a 16 A MCB will not blow instantly, but the bimetal finally gives way.

points.label: Magnetic trip
points.detail: A solenoid yanks the mechanism when current rises to several times the rating (a short-circuit). Magnetic trips are fast (milliseconds) where the bimetal protects slow overloads — that is why a 6 kA fault does not fry the cable.

points.label: Terminals
points.detail: Top = live coming in from the busbar. Bottom = live out to the circuit. Never swap them: the marking 'LINE' / 'LOAD' exists so the busbar side is always the same pole and the moving contacts stay off the busbar.

points.label: DIN-rail clip
points.detail: Two sprung prongs that snap over a 35 mm DIN rail. Pull the clip out with a screwdriver to release the breaker from the board without nudging its neighbours.

points.label: Rating window
points.detail: The stamped rating (16 A etc.) is the continuous current the breaker will carry and the ceiling of its overload protection. Match it to the cable size, not 'what the circuit might draw'.
